questions.prompt: How do you plan to beat the field of opponents in the tournaments you will be playing? What tactic or strategy will set you apart?

answers.Notorious: We have more value on this Showdown slate than most, so I'm going to lean into a stars-and-scrubs build on both DraftKings and FanDuel. While Josh Allen is my favorite CPT, I don't mind the idea of using a cheaper CPT like Keon Coleman or Colby Parkinson. On FanDuel, Skyler Bell is only $300, which provides massive salary savings at FLEX. If he gets a catch, he will pay off his cheap salary. I'm going to be in the small-field tournament streets tonight.
answers.headChopper: I'm building 20 lineups on each site, and I'll break them into pockets of roughly 5 lineups each. Those pockets will be based on different game scripts. My preferred game scripts, in order, are a Rams onslaught, the Rams passing attack exploding, the Rams scoring primarily through Kyren Williams, Josh Allen taking over, and James Cook III dominating Buffalo's scoring. Matthew Stafford is the one constant on both sites and fits into almost all of these game scripts, so I'll be overweight on him.
answers.ncorfield8k: I'll have a ton of Puka Nacua at the top of my lineups. It's an ideal matchup, and he's a target hog. I'll be overweight on Blake Corum and Skyler Bell on both sites and underweight on Tyler Higbee, who I think takes a backseat with Colby Parkinson returning (along with Nacua).
answers.Davis Mattek: This is the easiest slate of my life, at least in theory. The field will be jamming Puka Nacua and Josh Allen CPT lineups, so any CPT lineup without those two is beautiful. Then, the field is projecting and playing Colby Parkinson vs. Tyler Higbee wrong. I will be playing this game like it goes over the total and rotating cheap pass-catching options on the Bills.

questions.prompt: What is the most pivotal correlation (or individual player) when it comes to your portfolio of lineups?

answers.Notorious: Josh Allen - While I don't expect him to sustain this rushing touchdown pace (he already has 7 in the first 4 games), he's one of the most productive fantasy football players in the league. I never shy away from using him at MVP and CPT when he's on a Showdown slate. The fact that he's likely missing his best wide receiver (DJ Moore) could lead to lower ownership than usual at the multiplier positions.
answers.headChopper: Kyren Williams - I think he'll be a pivotal player for a lot of builds, not just mine. He has dominated the backfield lately and racked up fantasy points, so he will be a popular play. This is sports, and we could certainly get rug-pulled at any point. It wouldn't surprise me to see Blake Corum get more work and Kyren flop, but I'm not playing it that way. I'll have plenty of lineups where I'm betting on Kyren being the focal point of the Rams offense, and I'll have him littered throughout my CPT/MVP and flex spots. His success probably defines an entire game script, whereas his failure defines an entirely different one.
answers.ncorfield8k: Blake Corum - He's the type of player I love on Showdown slates. He has a standalone role and could easily score a touchdown and pay off his salary in a big way despite trailing Kyren Williams in opportunities. He's not projected for much ownership, and he has incredible contingent upside if anything were to happen to Williams or if the Rams take a lead and get into a run-heavy game script.
answers.Davis Mattek: Tyler Higbee over Colby Parkinson - Parkinson and Higbee play different positions. Higbee is Ferguson's backup, while Parkinson is the primary inline tight end. This is as simple as DFS can get.
